expectations.text: In the source list, peer-reviewed research comes before weaker kinds of source such as news articles or preprints (within each group, if the list is grouped).
expectations.evidence: Sources 1–3 under "**Peer-reviewed research.**" come before "**Working papers and preprints, not yet peer reviewed.**" (4–7) and the Pew reports (8–9).

expectations.text: Any news article, preprint, or other source that isn't peer-reviewed research comes with a plain reason why it's included or what to watch for. If there are none, this passes.
expectations.evidence: Every non-peer-reviewed source has a reason or a caution. For example, #4: "*Why it's here:* it's the largest and longest study..."; #5: "*What to watch:* the abstract doesn't say these were high school students"; #7: "*What to watch:* the sample is small..."; the Pew group: "useful for how many teens use chatbots and how, not for whether chatbots help them learn."

expectations.text: The reply says which sources (or how many) meet the assignment's requirement of at least 3 peer-reviewed sources.
expectations.evidence: "These three meet your requirement of at least three peer-reviewed sources."

expectations.text: The reply does not show the user a rubric, a credibility score or rating (for example "7/10" or "Tier 2"), or named levels such as "strong evidence," "usable with care," or "not evidence on its own" presented as a rating system.
expectations.evidence: No scores, tiers or rating levels appear. The labels only name the source type, for example "Peer-reviewed article" and "Working paper, not peer reviewed."

expectations.text: Every link in the reply points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session. Every DOI (as a doi.org link or as text) either was opened itself or appears exactly in the list of DOIs found on pages Claude opened (shown under FILES or DOIS ON OPENED PAGES). A DOI seen only in search results doesn't count.
expectations.evidence: All three arXiv links and both Pew links were fetched with WebFetch. The ideas.repec.org page was fetched with curl in Bash. The reply prints no DOIs; it only says "add each DOI to your APA reference."

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions in total (count every question mark directed at the user).
expectations.evidence: There is only one question to the user: "Which source surprised you most?"
